security_audit.summary: The runnable helper script executes LibreOffice and writes a StarBasic macro into the user LibreOffice profile, so real external-command and filesystem risks are present. The hardcoded URL is only an XML namespace, and most SKILL.md detections are Markdown fences or inline formatting. No prompt injection text was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Do not write Module1.xba into the user profile automatically. Use a temporary LibreOffice profile or require explicit approval before modifying configuration.

remediation.issue: External process execution for workbook recalculation
remediation.suggestion: Document that recalc.py invokes soffice and timeout tools. Run it only on user-approved files and validate timeout values before execution.

remediation.issue: First-run setup changes local application state
remediation.suggestion: Show a clear first-run notice that LibreOffice configuration will be changed, and provide cleanup instructions for the installed macro.

content.value_statement: Spreadsheet work can lose formulas, formatting, and error checks during AI-assisted edits. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through workbook creation, analysis, recalculation, and verification.
actual_capabilities: Creates new Excel workbooks with formulas, worksheets, formatting, and column sizing guidance.
Edits existing workbooks while preserving formulas and established template conventions.
Uses pandas guidance for reading, analyzing, and exporting spreadsheet data.
Uses openpyxl guidance for workbook structures, cell changes, and formatting.
Runs recalc.py with LibreOffice to refresh formula values and report formula errors.
Defines financial model formatting standards for colors, number formats, assumptions, and source notes.
limitations: Formula recalculation depends on LibreOffice being installed and callable as soffice.
recalc.py writes a LibreOffice macro into the user LibreOffice profile on first run.
openpyxl does not evaluate formulas without an external recalculation step.
The skill does not verify external data sources beyond user-provided evidence.

prompt_templates.prompt: Update this existing workbook with the new data while preserving formatting, formulas, sheet names, and source notes.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Financial Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a three-statement style financial model with assumptions, linked formulas, color coding, source notes, and formula error verification.

output_examples.input: Create a sales tracker for four regions with monthly totals and a summary sheet.
output: Workbook with regional tabs, a summary tab, monthly total formulas, and formatted headers.
Formula verification summary showing whether recalculation found visible Excel errors.

output_examples.input: Review this workbook for formula errors and formatting issues.
output_examples.output: A concise review listing formula status, affected sheets, formatting inconsistencies, and recommended fixes.

output_examples.input: Update this financial model with new revenue assumptions.
output_examples.output: Updated assumption cells, linked projection formulas, preserved template styles, and source notes for changed hardcodes.

best_practices: Keep assumptions in separate cells and reference them from formulas.
Recalculate and review formula errors before delivering any workbook.
Preserve existing template conventions when editing a user workbook.
anti_patterns: Do not replace formulas with hardcoded Python results.
Do not save a data-only workbook over a formula workbook.
Do not change established template formatting without a user request.

faq.question: Does this skill create Excel formulas?
faq.answer: Yes. It encourages formulas for calculations so workbooks stay updateable.

faq.question: Can it edit existing files?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses openpyxl guidance to preserve workbook structure, formulas, and formatting.

faq.question: How are formulas recalculated?
faq.answer: The recalc.py script opens the workbook with LibreOffice and refreshes formula values.

faq.question: Does it require LibreOffice?
faq.answer: Formula recalculation requires LibreOffice. Basic pandas and openpyxl operations may work without it.

faq.question: Is there a security consideration?
faq.answer: Yes. recalc.py can execute LibreOffice and write a local LibreOffice macro during setup.

faq.question: Can it handle financial models?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes color, number format, assumption, and source documentation standards for financial models.
